title: Papeleria comic manifest
description: A web comic in the studio's Web Comics format, schema version 1: at least one page of art in reading order, each with its alternative text, credit and rights, and the panels a reader steps through. Every panel carries a transcript, so the story reaches a reader who cannot see the art.

schema.description: The manifest format this piece is written for. Write 1. A missing, non-integer or smaller value is a manifest error; a larger one needs a newer Papeleria.

template.description: Which template builds this piece. This schema describes the comic template, so the value is comic.

title.description: The comic's title, shown in the register and used as the page title. Inline Markdown.

language.description: en (the default) or es. Sets the page language and chooses English or Spanish control labels. The editor itself stays English.

status.description: draft (the default), review, published or withheld. It is shown on the piece. published turns an unfilled [placeholder] into an error; withheld builds a private preview and writes nothing to dist/.

wordmark.description: The wordmark text for this piece. Leave it out to use the theme's, papeleria unless the owner has set another.

credits.description: The credits for the comic, shown on its last page in meta size.

format.description: The format label in the register. It defaults to Web Comics, or Web Cómics when the language is es.

pages.description: The pages in reading order, left to right: at least one and at most 1,000. Page N can be linked to as #page-N.

page.description: One page of art. A page carries its image fields directly, because every page has exactly one image. It has alternative text and is never decorative.

image.description: The page art under assets/images/, for example assets/images/pages/01.png. The original is kept for zoom details.

alt.description: What the page shows, for a reader who cannot see it. A comic page cannot be marked decorative.

credit.description: Who made the page art. A missing credit is a warning, separate from missing rights.

rights.description: The terms you hold the page art under. Missing rights is a warning, separate from a missing credit.

panels.description: The panels in reading order. Screen readers and the guided view follow this order; panel M of page N can be linked to as #page-N-panel-M. A page may have none.
